entries.title: A run-walk test for coming back to running
changes: At 60% of a running hold, a three-day test: a short run-walk, then how walking feels the next day, then stairs. A good result offers to start winding the hold down; anything else tries again in a week.
End on the ride screen now ends the whole ride: the workout and the route together.
Music settings show only what works today: Plex, OpenSubsonic and your own music files. Apple Music and iBroadcast are marked as not available yet.
Fixed: video playback no longer builds up in memory, and Apple Music no longer repeats its event handlers.
The Hub now tells you when an update is out (checked at most twice a day; you can turn it off here).

entries.title: The run-walk test for your assistant
changes: Added run_walk_test: your assistant can walk you through the three days and record each answer.
Assistant instructions match the new test and the End-ride behaviour.

entries.title: Morning inspiration and a visible update history

entries.title: The first public release
changes: The repository began its public history as a stationary-bike training hub.
During the following week it grew into a shared place for coaching, multisport load, recovery and program planning.

in_the_works.title: Your music folder
in_the_works.detail: Choose a music folder once and the Hub streams it on the ride screen, with no server to set up and no reselecting files after a reload.

in_the_works.title: Apple Music and iBroadcast
in_the_works.detail: Waiting on the Hub's app registration with each service.

in_the_works.title: Programs that adapt to you
in_the_works.detail: Recovery and progression driven by your measured response and check-ins rather than fixed waits, across every sport you train.

in_the_works.title: Lifting built on joints and movement directions
in_the_works.detail: Three full-body sessions (A, B, C) covering every joint action and direction, repeated and progressed for 4-6 weeks.

in_the_works.title: Likes, dislikes and learned rules
in_the_works.detail: Thumbs up or down on exercises after a workout; exercises you keep skipping come up less.
